places.name: Băng Tê Nguyên
places.size: A high tundra plateau at true scale, tens of kilometres across, with about 12 huge boulders scored by horns and a network of trenches several kilometres long; no buildings, at most a distant hunter's cairn.
places.where: Region 3, plateau of Thanh Loan Lĩnh at about 330 m, tundra. On the map a hazy blue-grey and ochre mottled tundra, grey mountains and a dark blue lake at the top, a green forested slope at the right. Beast lair, ice rhinoceroses (yêu cốt prize), belonging to no sect. Nearest: Tùng Linh Mạch spirit vein 226 km.
places.imagined: A low gold sun over a vast plateau, the deep rhino trenches casting blue shadows, huge grey boulders polished by horns, and a herd as dark specks crossing far away.
places.subject: The place: Băng Tê Nguyên, the Plain of the Ice Rhinoceroses, a high flat tundra plateau. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a high flat plateau of snow-dusted tundra, tawny lichen and pale scree runs across the frame to every edge, with a grey mountain wall and a dark blue lake at the upper left corner, a forested slope falling away at the right edge, pockets of frozen pools glinting. Signature element: a network of deep trenches trodden through the snow by heavy beasts, each a few metres deep and ten metres wide, running for kilometres in curving parallel lines and joining and splitting like braided rivers, with fresh packed snow at their bottoms and long blue shadows inside; scattered along the trenches stand about a dozen huge grey boulders the size of houses, each scored with long pale horn-gouges and polished smooth on its sides, ringed by trampled dark ground. At the base: lichen pockets in rust and olive, a frozen pool with cracked ice. A herd of about twenty ice rhinoceroses, grey-white armoured beasts with a single long horn, shown as tiny specks, one rubbing against a boulder, others crossing in line along a trench in the far distance; a thin mist of breath over them. No buildings; a tiny cairn of stones on a ridge with one hunter specks watching from far off. Light and season: late autumn afternoon, low golden light from the upper left raking over the trenches and polished stones, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hộ Lâm Đường
places.size: A forest-wardens' hall of about 45 wardens, raftsmen and seedbed hands (founded 910): a long low hall of unbarked logs with about 30 outbuildings, seedbeds and a river boom within about 300 m; looks like a lumber camp, and is one.
places.where: Region 3, edge of the northern woods, temperate forest at about 140 m; on the map a vast carpet of dark conifer forest with a river winding down from the upper right, a pale clearing at the upper left. Vassal of Thúy Vi Tông, Wood 48 %, Water 17 %. Nearest: Phi Thử Lâm beast lair 125 km, Độc Phong Cốc 168 km.
places.imagined: Spring flood morning. Logs, each asked first, are being sent down the river under a green banner, the boom is full, and wardens stand beside the hall in the mist.
places.subject: The place: Hộ Lâm Đường, the Forest-Warden Hall, a timber hall at the edge of the northern woods. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a vast carpet of dark conifer forest fills the frame to the edges, a river winding down through it from the upper right as a bright ribbon in spring flood, a pale clearing at the upper left. The hall: in a clearing on the river bank a long, low hall of unbarked logs about sixty metres long with a deep roof of grey shingle, a lean-to wing and a covered porch, surrounded by about thirty outbuildings, bunkhouses, a smithy for saws and axes, drying sheds, a mess hall, a small shrine with one roof, and a few rows of seedbeds in neat strips planted with thousands of tiny green saplings. Signature element: on the river a wide log boom, a floating fence of chained logs, with several hundred squared and unsquared logs gathered behind it, and rafts of lashed logs under green banners (cloth without symbols) being pushed out into the current by pole men, a long line of rafts already drifting downstream into the forest. At the forest edge beside the hall a few giant spirit trees stand marked with a strip of green cloth tied round the trunk, each with a tiny figure sitting vigil at its foot. Life at scale: raftsmen with long poles, wardens walking in line carrying saplings, a mule team hauling logs on a skid road, smoke from the cookhouse. Light and season: spring flood morning, golden light from the upper left through mist rising off the river, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Cổ Dịch Trấn (Thúy Vi Tông's new seat)
places.size: Since 1001-1006 the seat of a great alchemy sect: a domain about 4 km across in deep forest with no walls, about 70 palace-sized and smaller wooden halls, 300 or more lesser buildings in the old post town's grid, herb gardens and the Green Furnace; about 250 members and several thousand residents with servants, artisans, herb families and pilgrims.
places.where: Region 3, north-western hills, temperate forest at about 290 m, a former town (lived 520-980), the Old Post Town. On the map a dense dark forest with a pale rocky ridge across the lower middle and a pale clearing in the middle ground at the upper right with a small pond, a bay in the upper left corner. Wood 38 %, Earth 18 %, where the haze pools thickest. Nearest: Thương Thúy Lâm 146 km, Lam Yên Thị 182 km, the old seat 202 km.
places.imagined: Early morning, the green haze lying thick over the clearing so the great wooden halls stand in it half drowned. The Green Furnace is lit, the inn gardens grow too well, and the herb terraces climb the forest edge.
places.subject: The place: Thúy Vi Tông's new seat at Cổ Dịch Trấn, a great alchemy sect's wooden halls in deep forest and green haze, with no walls. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a dense dark forest of old conifer and broadleaf fills the frame, a pale rocky ridge with scree crossing the lower middle, a small bay of blue water in the upper left corner, and in the middle a broad clearing of luminous green meadow and garden. A blue-green haze pools thickest over the clearing, filling it like a bowl, with the tops of the tallest halls poking out. The seat: no wall encloses it; instead the old post town's grid of streets, grown over by gardens, holds about three hundred lesser buildings of weathered timber with green-glazed roofs, former inns and storehouses now dormitories, workshops and drying houses, buried in overgrown inn gardens of osmanthus and herbs that grow far too well; among them stand about seventy larger halls of dark wood, palace-sized with tiered roofs, the Haze Hall at the centre, a very long pill hall, scripture halls, a tower of seven roofs, linked by covered galleries and raised boardwalks over the gardens. Signature element: the Green Furnace, a huge round furnace hall of green bronze and wood about forty metres across, its roof an open ring through which a column of pale green fire-smoke rises and spreads into the haze, with a ring of smaller furnace houses around it; and the herb terraces of the sect cut in green stripes up the forest edge. Life at scale: tiny disciples in pale green carrying baskets of herbs, long lines of porters and herb carts on the road from the south, steam from the drying houses. Light and season: misty early morning in late spring, soft golden light from the upper left through the haze, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Vân Gian Trấn
places.size: A ruined mountain town of about 200 buried and half-buried houses in a footprint of about 500 m by 300 m, once perhaps 800 roofs; destroyed by an avalanche and left to the dead; empty, silent.
places.where: Region 3, high mountain at about 780 m on a steep forested slope among bare rock ridges. On the map a rugged mountain land of grey ridges and scree among dark conifer forest, with bare pockets and a pale road at the lower right. Former town, held by Thúy Vi Tông, Metal 26 %, Wood 22 %; left to the avalanche's dead. Nearest: Ngọc Trụ Phong peak 90 km, Nhạn Hồi Phong 100 km. A second slide buried the prior Mâu Hành Đáo.
places.imagined: A cold grey afternoon. A great tongue of grey rock debris covers half the town, roofs standing out of it at angles, the other half hung with grass and moss, and a lone cairn on the debris where someone dug.
places.subject: The place: Vân Gian Trấn, the Town among the Clouds, a mountain town buried by avalanches. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a steep mountain valley of grey rock ridges, scree and dark conifer forest, with bare rock walls at both sides and a high saddle at the upper edge, a pale narrow road at the lower right climbing the valley. The ruin: on a shelf of gentler slope in the middle, about two hundred houses of stone and timber with grey tile roofs in tiers up the valley's side, the lower half buried under a huge tongue of grey broken rock and splintered trees that poured from a raw scar high on the mountain, roofs sticking out of the debris at tilted angles, a pagoda leaning with its top storeys sheared off; the upper half stands, roofless and empty, grass in the rooms and moss on the walls, a few streets still visible, and a ruined gate tower at the road. A second smaller slide scar runs beside the first, with fresh pale rock. Signature element: the debris tongue itself, the grey flood of broken stone with houses drowned in it, kilometres long near the top and spread across the whole town, and a tiny cairn of stones on top where someone has dug and a bunch of dried flowers lies. Life at scale: no inhabitants; one tiny figure standing at the cairn, a hawk circling, a goat on the upper ruins. Light and season: cold grey late afternoon in autumn, thin golden light from the upper left on the debris, long soft shadows toward the lower right, a few clouds clinging to the saddle.

places.name: Thủy Cùng Phong
places.size: A bare mountain peak about 1,190 m high and about 2 km across at its base, where the abbey's stream ends in a cleft; at most a small sitting-platform, a stone seat and a few tiny huts; no settlement.
places.where: Region 3, a peak on the west coast near the sea at about 1.2 km: on the map a mountain of grey rock and scree among forest ridges with a blue bay at the right and a river at the upper middle running to the sea. Metal 38 %, Water. Nearest: Vân Khởi Quán 79 km, Quan Lan Bảo ruin 90 km. The abbot's sitting place, the stream's end.
places.imagined: Late evening. A thin stream climbs the peak and vanishes in a cleft just below the summit, where the abbot has sat for a night, tiny figures kneeling in rows on a rock shelf, with clouds filling the valleys below.
places.subject: The place: Thủy Cùng Phong, Where the Water Ends, a bare mountain peak where a stream runs out. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a bare grey peak of broken rock and scree rises in the centre of the frame, ringed by ridges of dark conifer and pale rock, a wide blue bay at the lower right with a turquoise coast, and a thin silver river at the top running down to the sea. A mountain stream descends from a corrie below the summit, a thread of white water twisting down the rocks, then disappearing into a narrow cleft in the stone just under the summit, ending abruptly. Signature element: at the cleft a flat rock shelf holds a small wooden sitting platform and a single worn stone seat with a few small flat sitting stones in rows, and about ten tiny figures in grey robes sit in a ring around the seat on the bare rock, one older figure in the middle; clouds rise from the valleys all around and have almost reached the shelf, so the peak seems an island in a white sea. A pale pilgrim's path of cairns winds up the peak from the lower left. Nothing else is built; a thin line of smoke from one tiny hut at the foot. Light and season: clear late evening in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the peak, the valleys filling with white cloud, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Tùng Đào Cung
places.size: A great sect seat, tier 1, founded 200: a domain about 7 km long on a ridge in an endless pine sea, about 400 buildings, palace-sized halls and a gallery 3 km long, about 300 members and several thousand residents (disciples, servants, artisans, pilgrims and families in the pine villages beneath).
places.where: Region 1/2, the Deep Pine Sea (Thâm Tùng Hải), temperate forest at about 810 m. On the map an endless dark forest, a long ridge of pale scree running through it, a river in the lower right with a blocky pale angular outline of a settlement beyond. Righteous great sect of Wood and Water spell cultivators, Wood 48 %, Water 16 %, lord of the pine sea, the river basin and the northern lake. Nearest: Thính Đào Nhãn spirit vein 75 km, Vân Tùng Lâm 182 km.
places.imagined: Low sun on a pine sea after rain. The great ridge rises out of dark green with stacked halls of dark timber and blue-grey tile, and the long roofed gallery along the crest runs out of sight, wind in the pines sounding in it like surf.
places.subject: The place: Tùng Đào Cung, the Palace of the Pine Waves, the great sect of Wood and Water. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; an endless sea of old pines fills the frame to every edge, dark green and blue-green in gentle waves, a river visible in the lower right as a thin bright ribbon, and rising out of it a long forested ridge running diagonally from lower left to upper right, about seven kilometres long, whose crest is crowned with the palace. The palace: some four hundred buildings of dark timber with blue-grey tile roofs on stepped terraces climbing the ridge, stacked pagoda halls of five and seven storeys, palace-sized halls on the upper shelves, long dormitories and lecture halls on the lower terraces, covered stairs and bridges over the ravines, all climbing to a great many-roofed main hall at the highest point, with a nine-storey tower beside it; pine trees grow between the halls and over their courtyards, never cut. Signature element: a long open-sided roofed gallery runs along the ridge crest from the main hall out into the pines for about three kilometres, its blue-grey tile roof a thin unbroken line that follows the ridge out of sight, with rows of tiny disciples sitting along it facing outward listening to the pines; the wind moves the pine crowns in visible waves around it. Villages of woodcutters, resin makers and pilgrims' inns sit in clearings at the ridge's foot, with smoke, and cart roads through the trees. Life at scale: hundreds of tiny robed figures on stairs and bridges, long lines of porters and pilgrims on the road, a group on the gallery. Light and season: late afternoon after rain, golden light from the upper left on the wet roofs and pine crowns, long soft shadows toward the lower right, mist rising from the valleys.

places.name: Vạn Hác Viện
places.size: An academy of sound cultivation of about 50 people (zither students, string-makers, wood-dryers), founded 620: about 45 grey-roofed halls along a ravine rim over about 400 m, and a single rock pillar about 60 m tall with a pavilion; compact, steep, vertical.
places.where: Region 1, deep pine sea ravines, temperate forest at about 840 m; on the map a forested mountain land of ravines with pale rocky ridges and a thin river at the upper left. Vassal of Tùng Đào Cung, Metal 48 %, Wood 24 %, keepers of the zither Tùng Phong Cầm. Nearest: Thạch Lục Khoáng 79 km, Bích Hác Sâm 90 km.
places.imagined: A windy afternoon. The ravine below the hexagonal pavilion sounds like a thousand zither strings, the students sit on the rim facing it, and long string-drying racks vibrate in the breeze.
places.subject: The place: Vạn Hác Viện, the Academy of Ten Thousand Ravines, a school of sound on a ravine rim. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a country of deep forested ravines, pale rock ridges and dark pine slopes fills the frame, a thin river winding at the upper left. The academy: about forty-five halls of grey stone and timber with grey tile roofs stepping along the rim of the deepest ravine in a long curve, a double gate hall, a long practice hall with a row of tall windows facing the ravine, dormitories, string-making sheds, wood-drying lofts with stacked sticks of seasoned timber, kitchens; stairs and terraces cut along the rim, small round platforms jutting over the edge. Signature element: in the middle of the ravine a single tall pillar of rock rises from the ravine floor about sixty metres to the level of the rim, topped by a small hexagonal pavilion with a double grey roof, joined to the rim by a long narrow plank bridge of timber; around the pillar the ravine opens in a dizzy pit with a faint pale mist at the bottom and the dark pine tops rising on the far side. Along the rim, long racks hold hundreds of silk strings stretched to dry, shining like threads of light in the sun, and a ring of tiny students sit cross-legged facing the ravine, each with a zither on the knees. Life at scale: a player on the pavilion, two students on the bridge, string-makers at the racks. Light and season: windy late-summer afternoon, golden light from the upper left on the grey roofs and the strings, long soft shadows toward the lower right, the ravine deep blue.

places.name: Tùng Gian Thành
places.size: A walled port city of about 22,000 roofs and perhaps 110,000 people, walls about 3 km by 2.3 km, at a river mouth, with pines growing inside the walls and a moon gate about 25 m wide in the wall facing the hills; the first city of Tùng Đào Cung.
places.where: Region 1, coast at a river mouth, sea level, temperate forest; on the map a deep bay of dark blue sea in the upper half between two forested headlands, with a river entering at the upper right. Tùng Đào Cung's first city and port, raised 240. Nearest: Thạch Thượng Tuyền spirit vein 79 km, Thanh Tùng Thôn 160 km.
places.imagined: Moonrise at the Night of a Thousand Pines. A lantern hangs on every tree around the city, and from the harbour road the moon rises framed in the huge round moon gate among the pines.
places.subject: The place: Tùng Gian Thành, the Pine Moon city, the port of the great sect Tùng Đào. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep bay of dark blue sea fills the upper half of the frame between two forested headlands, with a river entering at the upper right in a sandy delta, and a dense pine forest covering the land to the lower edge. The city: a great rectangular wall of grey stone about three kilometres long with a dozen gate towers, enclosing some twenty-two thousand grey-tile roofs in districts, a dense quay quarter of narrow streets and warehouses along the river mouth, a broad market district with timber yards and resin warehouses, a pilgrims' quarter of inns and shrines, a terrace district of courtyard mansions, and a great palace-style hall among the pines with beams carved from one fallen pine; and everywhere tall dark pines growing inside the walls, between the roofs and along the streets, never cut, buildings built around them. Signature element: in the wall facing the palace ridge stands a huge round moon gate about twenty-five metres wide, its circular opening framing pines and sky, and a straight avenue through it toward the hills; a faint blue-silver ring of formation light lies over the wall. Along the shore and quays about a hundred junks and barges, and thousands of tiny lantern points on every tree around the city. Life at scale: crowds on the quay, carts with pine timber, pilgrims queuing at the moon gate. Light and season: dusk of the autumn festival, last golden light from the upper left on the walls and treetops, lanterns glowing amber among the pines, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Tùng Hạ Thị
places.size: A market in a perfect ring of about 70 round stall-houses about 180 m in diameter, with a few hundred houses around it (woodcutters, carters, inns) and perhaps 2,000 residents; a market, not a city, in a clearing about 800 m across.
places.where: Region 1, pine sea clearing, temperate forest at about 180 m; on the map an endless pine forest, a pale clearing with a rocky patch in the middle left and a hill ridge at the lower right. Tùng Đào Cung market. Nearest: Tùng Âm Mạch spirit vein 175 km, Tùng Đào Cung 212 km, Tuần Tùng Đường 215 km. Pilgrims' tent ring since 205.
places.imagined: A busy market morning in a clearing of tall old pines. The perfect ring of round stall-houses is crowded, a single gate opens onto the forest road, and carts wait in line outside.
places.subject: The place: Tùng Hạ Thị, the Market beneath the Pines, a market in a perfect ring in a forest clearing. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a wide clearing of grass and old pine stumps among tall dark old pines, the forest dense to every edge, a pale rocky knoll at the left and a low forested ridge at the lower right, one forest road entering from the lower left. The market: a perfect ring of about seventy small round stall-houses with low grey cone roofs set shoulder to shoulder around an open circular yard about a hundred and eighty metres across, with one gap for a gate on the road side, the inside yard filled with awnings, a central well with a bell post, and crowded stalls in concentric rings; outside the ring, in the clearing, lie a loose scatter of woodcutters' houses, carters' yards with wagon rows, two long inns, a pilgrims' hostel and stacks of resin barrels and timber. Signature element: the ring itself, a clean grey wheel with a hub of market tents, the only geometric form in the whole pine sea, preserved from the pilgrims' original ring of tents. Life at scale: a long train of carts and pack mules on the road, hundreds of tiny shoppers inside the ring, a few cultivators in robes at the gate, children, woodsmen's oxen. Light and season: bright autumn morning, golden light from the upper left on the grey cone roofs, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Lộc Minh Trấn
places.size: A small walled timber town of about 1,200 roofs inside a wall about 500 m by 350 m, roughly 5,500 people, at a marshy river mouth with a ferry pier about 150 m long, famous for its carved beam ends.
places.where: Region 1, low marshy river mouth at sea level on the edge of the pine forest; on the map a wide bay of blue water at the lower left, forested land around, a thin river at the right. Held by Lãng Đạo Môn (a ferry guild). Nearest: Cự Thát Chử beast lair 79 km, Hổ Khiếu Trấn ruin 125 km, Lâu Thuyền Trấn 177 km.
places.imagined: Dawn. A life-sized carved stag stands at the end of the long ferry pier, head raised toward the water, and every beam end of the timber houses is carved with fine deer, leaves and clouds.
places.subject: The place: Lộc Minh Trấn, the Calling Stag town, a timber town at a river mouth where the carvers of the pine sea live. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a bay of blue water at the lower left with pale reed banks along a low marshy shore, a river winding in from the right, and pine forest rising behind the town to the upper left. The town: a small rectangular walled town about five hundred metres long, timber walls on a stone footing, twelve hundred grey-tile roofs of timber houses in tight rows around a central square, a ferry gate toward the water and a land gate to the forest road; a carvers' guild hall with a deep roof, workshops with stacked planks, a long timber yard; every beam end under every eave carved, so the roof edges look scalloped and ornate. Two flat ferry boats at a long stone-footed pier. Signature element: at the end of the long ferry pier, about a hundred and fifty metres out over the reeds, stands a life-sized stag carved from pine, head raised and antlers wide, pale gold against the grey water, tiny people at its feet; a second faint line of carved posts follows the pier. Life at scale: ferrymen poling flat boats, carvers at work in open yards, a cart with beams, a few real deer at the forest edge. Light and season: early morning in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the pier and the stag, mist rising off the reeds, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Cổ Độ Thành
places.size: A walled river city among bamboo groves, about 16,000 roofs and perhaps 80,000 people, walls about 2.6 km by 1.8 km, with a broad stone ferry stair about 60 m wide and a rusted iron chain link about 4 m tall; a ferry and smithing city.
places.where: Region 1/2, bank of the southern river, bamboo forest at about 140 m; on the map a forested valley with a river winding as a sharp-angled blue line through green bamboo meadow, pale yellow-green clearings at the lower left. Tùng Đào Cung city, founded 320. Nearest: Trúc Căn Mạch 75 km, Luyện Thiết Trấn ruin 90 km. Its ferrymen carried the iron chain for Thiết Tỏa Quan.
places.imagined: A busy afternoon. Two flat ferries cross, smithy smoke rises behind the bamboo, and ferrymen drag a long rusted chain link up the broad stair to a smith's cart.
places.subject: The place: Cổ Độ Thành, the Old Ferry city, a walled city among bamboo groves on the southern river. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a broad river winds across the frame in a sharply angled course, its water blue-green, green bamboo groves and pale grassy meadows fill both banks, and low forested hills rise at the upper left. The city: a rectangular wall of grey stone about two and a half kilometres long with gate towers, enclosing some sixteen thousand grey-tile roofs among bamboo clumps, a ferrymen's quarter at the river with tall stilt houses and boat sheds, a smithing district with dozens of smoking chimneys and forge yards, a grain and iron market, canals and bridges, a governor's compound; bamboo grows inside the walls between courtyards. Signature element: a broad stone ferry stair about sixty metres wide descends in wide steps into the river from the city's river gate, crowned at the top by a single huge rusted iron chain link, four metres tall, standing upright on a stone plinth, a dark red-brown ring against the grey stone; more links lie in rows on the stair where they have been djagged from the river, and a team of oxen hauls one. Two flat ferries cross the river with carts and crowds. Life at scale: hundreds of tiny porters and ferry crews, smiths at their forges, merchants on the quay. Light and season: bright afternoon in early autumn, golden light from the upper left on the stair and the link, long soft shadows toward the lower right, smithy smoke drifting.

places.name: Bạch Hoa Thôn
places.size: A coastal village of about 25 grey-roofed houses in a birch grove about 300 m across, perhaps 120 people, with a narrow beach and a small jetty.
places.where: Region 1, coast at sea level, temperate forest; on the map the north shore of a deep blue bay with forested headlands, a pale patch at the lower right. Tùng Đào village, Water, Wood. Nearest: Hỏa Tẫn Trấn ruin 125 km, Thạch Thượng Tuyền 177 km, Tùng Gian Thành 180 km. White birches grew where a forest fire had burned.
places.imagined: Bright autumn morning in a pied grove. White birch trunks mix with tall black charred stumps, a bark-drying rack stands at the beach, and no one will pull up the stumps.
places.subject: The place: Bạch Hoa Thôn, the White Flower village, a coastal village inside a grove of white birches among burned stumps. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; the north shore of a deep blue bay fills the upper part of the frame, a narrow pale beach along its edge, with forested headlands left and right and a dense stand of dark pines behind. The village: about twenty-five grey-tile houses of timber scattered in the grove along two footpaths, each with a small yard, a few bark-sheet drying frames, a small shrine and a small jetty with two boats at the beach. Signature element: the grove itself, slender white birch trunks mixed with hundreds of tall black charred stumps of older trees, a striking black-and-white pattern like a pied hide spread over the ground, the birch crowns bright yellow and the stumps scorched black against fallen golden leaves; a long bark-drying rack at the beach holds sheets of pale birch bark in rows. No stump has been pulled up. Life at scale: villagers stripping bark from standing birches with curved knives, a girl carrying a bundle of bark sheets, a dog, thin smoke from three chimneys. Light and season: bright autumn morning, golden light from the upper left lighting the white trunks and yellow leaves, long soft shadows toward the lower right. The beach is a narrow pale crescent with a line of dark seaweed at the tide mark, and the little jetty is made of grey weathered planks on stone piers. Behind the village a low bank is covered with fallen birch bark in curls, and a ring of stones stands before each door as a hearth, since the charcoal of the stumps is never burned in a house. A narrow path leads inland through the pied grove toward the pines.

places.name: Thanh Tùng Thôn
places.size: A river village of about 30 grey-roofed houses with a memorial pine grove of about 300 planted pines in exact rows, perhaps 140 people, in about 350 m.
places.where: Region 1, river bank by a bay, temperate forest at sea level; on the map a forested peninsula with a river winding down from the upper centre to the lower right. Tùng Đào village. Nearest: Cổ Cái Lâm forest 79 km, Thạch Thượng Tuyền 90 km, Tùng Gian Thành 160 km. Survivors of Hổ Khiếu Trấn planted a pine for each of their dead.
places.imagined: A quiet spring morning. Tall pines stand in ranks, each with a small flat pale stone at its foot, and families sweep the stones beneath their own trees.
places.subject: The place: Thanh Tùng Thôn, the Green Pine village, a river village beside a grove of pines planted in exact rows. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a green forested land fills the frame, a river winding down through it from the top centre to the lower right, and a blue bay at the upper left with a forested peninsula. The village: about thirty grey-tile houses on the river bank in a loose row of yards with gardens, a ferry landing with one flat boat, a small hall with a larger roof, drying racks and a few fish traps in the river. Signature element: beside the village a grove of about three hundred tall pines planted in exact straight rows running from the riverbank to the forest edge like ranks of soldiers, each tree with a small pale flat stone at its foot, so that the ground between the rows shows a regular dotted pattern of pale stones; a straight path runs between the rows and long straight shadows lie between them. The pines are tall now, thirty metres, with clean trunks. Between the village and the grove runs a low turf bank, and the river beside it is pale green with sky reflected. Life at scale: a dozen tiny villagers with brooms sweeping among the stones, an old woman sitting under one tree, a child laying a green sprig. Light and season: clear spring morning, golden light from the upper left throwing regular long shadows of the pines toward the lower right.

places.name: Tùng Phong Thôn
places.size: A small river village of about 20 grey-roofed houses with two huge pines carrying wind strings about 40 m long between them, perhaps 100 people, in about 250 m.
places.where: Region 1, river bank in pine forest, temperate forest at about 200 m; on the map a forest with a winding river and a pale yellow-green clearing at the left, rocky ridges at the upper right. Tùng Đào village; Vạn Hác Viện's zither students practise here. Nearest: Ban Hổ Lĩnh beast lair 79 km, Luyện Thiết Trấn ruin 103 km.
places.imagined: A windy afternoon. Long fine strings stretched between two great pines glint in the light and hum and moan in the wind, a sound that carries over the whole hamlet.
places.subject: The place: Tùng Phong Thôn, the Pine Wind village, a river village with wind strings strung between two great pines. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a pine forest fills the frame with a winding river crossing from the left to the lower middle, a pale green clearing at the left, grey rocky ridges at the upper right. The village: about twenty grey-tile houses on the river bank in a loose line, small garden plots, a shallow ford with stepping stones, a few students' cottages with a long practice shed. Signature element: at the village edge two great pines, each forty metres tall, stand about forty metres apart, and between them stretch dozens of long fine strings, glinting like silver threads in the light, tuned in rows from the highest branch to a lower one, and wind-shaped ripples run along them; a few tiny students sit on a bench below, listening. Life at scale: villagers sleeping on porches, children pointing at the strings, a student tuning with a key, a woman at the ford. Light and season: windy late afternoon, golden light from the upper left catching the strings, long soft shadows toward the lower right. On the far bank of the river a few goats graze a steep patch of grass, and a line of small boys fishes from the ford stones. Each house has a short fence of woven pine twigs and a stack of resinous firewood. The village's one lane is carpeted in brown needles, and the shadows of the two great trunks fall across the roofs; the garden plots at the river's edge are tiny squares of bright green against the dark forest floor, with the sky showing as a narrow pale gap above the river.

places.name: Thạch Lục Khoáng
places.size: A malachite mine of a few dozen workers: about 8 small mine mouths among the roots of giant old pines on a steep slope of about 600 m, with green spoil heaps; no buildings except a lean-to.
places.where: Region 1, high mountain slope at about 790 m, temperate forest; on the map a steep forested slope with pale rocky ridges and a thin river at the upper left. Malachite mine (xích đồng; Metal, Wood) held by Vạn Hác Viện. Nearest: Bích Hác Sâm 75 km, Vạn Hác Viện 79 km.
places.imagined: Afternoon light on a steep slope of giant old pines whose huge roots frame small dark tunnel mouths, bright green malachite spoil in heaps against the brown needles.
places.subject: The place: Thạch Lục Khoáng, the Green Stone Mine, a malachite mine tunnelled among the roots of giant pines. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a steep high slope of giant old pines with huge exposed roots fills the frame, pale rock ribs and a thin river at the upper left, brown needle litter covering the ground. Signature element: eight small dark mine mouths, each about two metres wide, open between the great exposed roots of the oldest pines, each shored with dressed stone and never with timber, and below each a heap of bright green malachite spoil, vivid as paint against the brown needles; the roots arch above the tunnel mouths like cathedral ribs. At the base: brown needle litter, a narrow mule path winding down the slope, a small lean-to shelter with a grey roof, stacked baskets. Human trace: about a dozen tiny miners with baskets coming out of tunnels, a mule train waiting on the path, a figure with a measuring cord marking a root so it is not cut. Light and season: clear autumn afternoon, warm golden light from the upper left on the green spoil, dappled shadows under the pines, long soft shadows toward the lower right. Fallen pine cones and brown needles blanket the slope in a thick soft layer, and the roots, some as thick as a house's beams, arch across the ground and over the spoil paths in every direction. Small carts on stone-lined tracks lead from each mine mouth to one collecting yard where the ore is sorted by colour into heaps, deep green, pale green and blue-green, each heap covered with a hide against rain. The forest above the slope is dense and dark.

places.name: Thương Tùng Mạch
places.size: A high summit about 1.4 km above the sea with a grove of about 60 ash-grey pines inside an old fence about 300 m across, a narrow guarded path and a few guard huts; no settlement.
places.where: Region 2, high mountain at about 1.4 km above the pine sea, on the map a rocky ridge of pale rock and scree with green pine slopes and tawny alpine grass. A wild spirit vein (Metal, Earth) fenced and guarded by Tùng Đào Cung, 4 tiles from the border with Thiên Xu. Nearest: Hôi Thiết Khoáng mine 79 km, Phi Thử Nhai 146 km.
places.imagined: A high summit above the roaring pine sea. A grove of ash-grey pines stands still inside an old fence of stone posts, the air inside perfectly calm, a few disciples cultivating in turns.
places.subject: The place: Thương Tùng Mạch, the Grey Pine Vein, a grove of ash-grey pines on a high summit. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a high rocky summit of pale grey rock and scree rises from an endless dark pine sea at the upper left, ridges of grey rock running diagonally across the frame, tawny alpine grass and low shrubs on the shelves, thin shadow lines of ravines. At the middle of the frame lies a summit plateau. Signature element: on the plateau stands a grove of about sixty pines whose bark is the colour of ash, older and paler than any trees around, their crowns thin and silvery, ringed by an old fence of weathered stone posts and timber rails about three hundred metres around; the grove is a still, pale island and the air above it is calm, while the pines below the summit are tossed by wind in visible waves. Inside the fence the ground has a faint ring of paler stone laid over the vein. At the base: bare rock, a narrow guarded path climbing from the forest in a zigzag to a small gate in the fence, with two small guard huts with grey roofs. Human trace: four tiny disciples sitting cross-legged in a row on flat stones under the pines, two guards at the gate. Light and season: clear high-altitude morning in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the ash-grey trunks, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hổ Khiếu Trấn
places.size: A ruined forest town of about 600 once-roofs, now about 200 mossy wall lines in a footprint of about 500 m by 300 m, on a river bend; abandoned since the beast tide of 734.
places.where: Region 1, deep pine forest on a river bend by a lake or bay at about sea level; on the map a lake of dark blue water at the left, forested land around, a river winding to it. Former town held by Tùng Đào Cung, never resettled. Nearest: Cự Thát Chử beast lair 75 km, Lộc Minh Trấn 125 km. Its survivors' children live at Thanh Tùng Thôn; a tiger still dens in the old magistrate's hall.
places.imagined: A grey afternoon. Moss covers the low town walls, young trees grow in the streets, a timber watchtower lies toppled across the gate scored with claw gouges as long as a man, and a tiger lies in the old hall.
places.subject: The place: Hổ Khiếu Trấn, the Tiger's Roar town, a ruin on a river bend in a deep pine forest. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; deep dark pine forest fills the frame, a dark blue lake at the left with a pale reed shore, and a river bend curling around the ruin. The ruin: the low moss-covered walls of a small town, a rough rectangle about five hundred metres long, its palisade fallen and its stone footing green with moss, roofless timber houses in rows with young trees and bracken growing in the streets and through the floors, a broader magistrate's hall with a sagging ridge at the centre in whose doorway something tawny lies, a pale road leading to the gate. Signature element: a tall timber watchtower, thirty metres long, lies toppled across the gateway, its beams scored with huge pale claw gouges, long as a man is tall, in sets of four; a heap of bones, pale in the grass, beside the gate. Life at scale: no people; a tiny tiger lying on the hall steps, two crows, a deer at the forest edge. Light and season: grey, cool afternoon in autumn, thin golden light from the upper left on the moss and the toppled tower, long soft shadows toward the lower right. The river bend shows a pale gravel bar beside the ruin where the ford once crossed, now overgrown with willow scrub, and a few rotted timbers of the old landing stick out of the bank. Inside the wall line the paved main street is a dark strip of moss, and the old stone well in the square is capped by a young alder. A few tall pines have already grown through the roofs of the larger houses, their crowns above the old ridgelines.

places.name: Thiết Tỏa Quan
places.size: A ruined fort of about 40 broken buildings and a wall about 300 m long on a forested bluff, built in 503 for a siege; a stone anchor block about 6 m wide at the bluff's edge; empty, never rebuilt.
places.where: Region 1/2, forested bluff above the river road at about 570 m; on the map a dark forested mountain land with pale rock ridges running diagonally and a river at the upper left. Former fort of Tùng Đào and Lạc Hà in the War of the Pivot, broken by Thiên Xu; held by Tùng Đào Cung. Nearest: Quan Hạ Thôn 75 km, Tỏa Thiết Khoáng 103 km, Hôi Thiết Khoáng 158 km.
places.imagined: Late afternoon. A great snapped iron ring hangs from a stone anchor block at the bluff's edge, rust-red against grey stone and green forest, the broken gate towers behind it, and far below the river runs.
places.subject: The place: Thiết Tỏa Quan, the Iron Chain Pass, the ruin of a fort on a forested bluff above a river. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a forested bluff of dark pine with pale rock ridges running diagonally across the frame, a river running along the foot of the bluff at the upper left as a thin bright ribbon with a pale road beside it. The fort: a rectangle of cracked grey stone walls about three hundred metres long on the bluff top, about forty broken buildings of stone and timber with roofs fallen in, barracks lines and storehouses with collapsed ridges, a broken gate on the road side with one tower still standing and broken-topped and the other fallen in a heap of stone, the parade ground overgrown with grass and small trees. Signature element: at the bluff's very edge a massive square stone anchor block, about six metres wide, holds a great iron ring, snapped open, rust-red against the grey stone, from which the thousand-fathom chain once ran across the river; below it, in the river's pale shallows, a faint line of links lies sunk across the whole river bed as dark beads, and a few tiny figures stand in the river dragging a link. Life at scale: a few tiny people, a mule and cart on the road below, otherwise empty. Light and season: late afternoon in early autumn, warm golden light from the upper left striking the rust-red ring and the grey stone, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Bạch Viên Lĩnh
places.size: A forested ridge about 15 km long among pale rock outcrops and crags, with a troop of about 60 white apes; no buildings, at most a tiny herb-gatherers' hut and a cairn at the edge.
places.where: Region 1/2, mountains at about 1.05 km, temperate forest; on the map dense pine forest with grey and white rock outcrops scattered through it like islands. Beast lair, white apes, belonging to no sect. Nearest: Thải Sâm Trấn ruin 75 km, Tiều Phu Thôn village 106 km.
places.imagined: A misty morning on the ridge. A troop of white apes sits on the crags among the pines, the pale rock outcrops and the apes' fur barely distinguishable, and a lone herb-gatherer climbs far below.
places.subject: The place: Bạch Viên Lĩnh, the Ridge of the White Apes, a forested crag-land that holds a troop of white apes. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; an unbroken carpet of dense pine and mixed forest fills the frame, rolling in ridges, with pale grey and white rock outcrops and tors rising through it like islands, some with sheer faces, glades of yellow-green grass between them, and a few thin streams. Signature element: on the crags and pale outcrops about sixty white apes, tiny pale specks the colour of the rock, sit in groups of five and ten along the ledges, grooming and watching, with a large silver-white old male on the highest rock; their pale fur nearly blends with the pale stone so the eye must hunt for them, and faint trails of broken branches and fur-tufted bark mark their routes through the canopy between outcrops. A few tiny black pools of shadow mark cave mouths on the rock faces. No buildings: only at the very lower left edge of the frame a tiny herb-gatherer's hut with a stack of baskets, a cairn and one small figure with a basket looking up. Light and season: misty early morning in late summer, golden light from the upper left on the pale outcrops, long soft shadows toward the lower right, thin mist in the hollows. The glades between the outcrops are carpeted in yellow-green grass with wild flowers in small pockets, and thin streams run through them, glinting. The white apes' fur is matched by the pale trunks of birches growing on the rock ledges, and old tracks of their passage, bent saplings and scuffed moss, thread from outcrop to outcrop in long curves. Far below the ridge a thin thread of road marks the world of people, with the herb-gatherer's hut a small grey roof beside it.
